english: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers and let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by
Suppose that $f$ is continuous at $x=-1$ and that $f$ is differentiable at some point $c\neq-1$. Then the value of $a+b$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $a$ तथा $b$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं तथा $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ इस प्रकार परिभाषित है कि $x$ परिमेय होने पर $f(x)=x^{3}$ तथा $x$ अपरिमेय होने पर $f(x)=ax+b$ है।
माना कि $f$, $x=-1$ पर सतत है तथा $f$ किसी बिन्दु $c\neq-1$ पर अवकलनीय है। तब $a+b$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Rationals and irrationals are dense, so $f$ is continuous at $x_0$ iff $x_0^{3}=ax_0+b$, i.e. iff $x_0$ is a root of $q(x)=x^{3}-ax-b$
Differentiable at $c$: difference quotients along rationals $\to3c^{2}$, along irrationals $\to a$; so $q(c)=0$ and $a=3c^{2}$, i.e. $q'(c)=0$: $c$ is a repeated root
Roots of $q$: $-1,c,c$ with $c\neq-1$; no $x^{2}$ term $\Rightarrow -1+2c=0\Rightarrow c=\frac12$
solution_full: Every interval contains rationals and irrationals. If $x_0^{3}\neq ax_0+b$, then near $x_0$ the values of $f$ approach two different numbers, so $f$ is discontinuous at $x_0$. If $x_0^{3}=ax_0+b$, both pieces tend to the same value and $f$ is continuous at $x_0$.
So $f$ is continuous exactly at the real roots of $q(x)=x^{3}-ax-b$. Continuity at $-1$ gives $q(-1)=0$, i.e. $-1+a-b=0$.

Differentiability at $c$ requires continuity, so $q(c)=0$. Then for rational $x\to c$: $\dfrac{f(x)-f(c)}{x-c}=\dfrac{x^{3}-c^{3}}{x-c}\to3c^{2}$; for irrational $x\to c$: $\dfrac{ax+b-(ac+b)}{x-c}=a$. Both limits must agree, so $a=3c^{2}$. Conversely, if $q(c)=0$ and $a=3c^{2}$, both quotients tend to $3c^{2}$ and $f'(c)=3c^{2}$.
$a=3c^{2}$ means $q'(c)=3c^{2}-a=0$, so $c$ is a repeated root of $q$.
$q$ is a cubic with roots $-1$ and the repeated root $c\neq-1$, so its roots are $-1,c,c$. The coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $q$ is $0$, so $-1+2c=0$ and $c=\dfrac12$.
originality_note: New: for a function given by different formulas on rationals and irrationals, continuity points are the roots of x^3 - ax - b and differentiability points are its repeated roots, so 'continuous at -1 and differentiable elsewhere' pins the cubic by Vieta (way 5). Closest known: f = x on Q, 1-x on Q^c is continuous only at 1/2. Different because: differentiability (tangency of the two formulas) is required and the root structure determines a and b.
key_step: Differentiability at c needs q(c) = 0 and a = 3c^2, i.e. a repeated root; Vieta then gives c = 1/2.
justification: A routine chain of three steps (continuity iff equal formulas, derivative match along both sets, Vieta) built on the familiar rational/irrational continuity idea. Comparable to 2024-P1-Q1 (L2) in length; the tangency step keeps it from L1.

concept_use.Continuity and Differentiability of func: f is defined by x^3 on the rationals and ax + b on the irrationals; continuity needs the two formulas to agree and differentiability needs their derivatives to agree as well.

stem_review: Read as a student: a, b and f (domain, codomain, both cases) are defined; 'differentiable at some point c not equal to -1' excludes the other solution a = 3, b = 2 (differentiable at -1). Checked with sympy that the system has exactly these two solutions. Answer 0.50, a decimal between 0 and 1. Changed: wrote 'x rational' inside text in the cases block.
